s: Methods, status codes, headers, HTTPS, CORS
d: HTTP is the protocol behind every web request. Understanding methods, status codes, headers, cookies, and the request-response cycle is fundamental. You'll deal with HTTP literally every day as a backend developer.
c: Methods: GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE OPTIONS HEAD

p: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is the foundation of data communication on the web. It is a stateless, application-layer protocol running over TCP/IP.
1. Client sends Request (Method, URI, Headers, Body).
3. Server sends Response (Status Code, Headers, Body).
4. Connection is closed (HTTP/1.0) or kept alive (HTTP/1.1).

POST /api/login HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"username": "admin", "password": "123"}

[ Client ]                        [ Server ]
   | --- GET /users (Headers) -----> |
   |                                 | (DB Query)
   | <--- 200 OK (JSON Body) ------- |
   
Stateless: Server forgets client immediately after response.
